introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Commerce 2 (0520), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer any FOUR questions. All questions carry equal marks.

Instructions: 1. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. 2. The use of SIMPLE electronic calculator is allowed. 3. Show clear working in your answer booklet where necessary.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde impose « Answer any FOUR questions. All questions carry equal marks ». Le sujet imprime 6 questions, sans sections : `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné (2 pages : page de garde, puis les six questions sur une seule page) ; filigranes (gcerevision.com) ignorés. Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées. Les chiffres des exemples (CFAF) sont hypothétiques ; aucune statistique réelle, loi, taux ou institution n'est avancé au-delà des notions du programme.

Points : le sujet n'imprime que les points de chaque sous-question, jamais le total ; `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide. Les points imprimés totalisent 20 par question (Q1 : 8+6+6 ; Q2 : 6+6+8 ; Q3 : 6+8+6 ; Q4 : 8+8+4 ; Q5 : 6+6+8, la sous-question (c) n'ayant aucun point imprimé ; Q6 : 8+8+4), conformément à « All questions carry equal marks » : aucun écart de total.

Question 4(a) : écart dans les données imprimées. Stock initial + achats - stock final = 150,000 + 400,000 - 50,000 = 500,000, alors que le tableau imprime un coût des marchandises vendues de 600,000. Le corrigé utilise la valeur imprimée (600,000) comme le sujet la donne : marge brute 150,000 (25 % de 600,000), ventes 750,000, bénéfice net 100,000, marge sur ventes 20 %, rotation 6 fois. Avec 500,000 on aurait 125,000 ; 75,000 ; 20 % ; 5 fois. Les données du sujet ne sont pas corrigées.

Question 4(a) : le taux de marque (mark-up) de 25 % est appliqué au coût des marchandises vendues (sens usuel du mark-up) ; la rotation du stock est calculée sur le stock moyen (coût des marchandises vendues / stock moyen).

Question 4(c) : les noms exacts des services de l'État ne sont pas avancés (aucune institution précise nommée) ; le corrigé parle de ministère ou service chargé du commerce, de la santé publique, de la normalisation, des poids et mesures, des douanes.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The table below shows extracts from the accounting records of NDOLO Enterprise at the end of a trading period.

| Particulars | Amount (CFAF) |
|---|---:|
| Opening stock | 150,000 |
| Closing stock | 50,000 |
| Cost of goods sold | 600,000 |
| Purchases | 400,000 |
| Working expenses | 50,000 |
| Mark-up | 25% |

You are required to calculate;

i) Gross Profit,

ii) Net profit,

iii) Gross profit as a percentage of sales.

iv) Rate of turnover.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The mark-up is a percentage of the **cost of goods sold** (the cost price): $\text{mark-up} = \dfrac{\text{gross profit}}{\text{cost of goods sold}} \times 100$.

**i) Gross profit**

$$\text{Gross profit} = \text{mark-up \%} \times \text{cost of goods sold} = \dfrac{25}{100} \times 600{,}000 = 150{,}000$$

Gross profit = **CFAF 150,000**.

**Sales** (needed for part iii) = cost of goods sold + gross profit = 600,000 + 150,000 = CFAF 750,000.

**ii) Net profit**

$$\text{Net profit} = \text{gross profit} - \text{working expenses} = 150{,}000 - 50{,}000 = 100{,}000$$

Net profit = **CFAF 100,000**.

**iii) Gross profit as a percentage of sales**

$$\dfrac{\text{gross profit}}{\text{sales}} \times 100 = \dfrac{150{,}000}{750{,}000} \times 100 = 20\%$$

Gross profit is **20%** of sales (this is the margin; it is different from the mark-up of 25% because the mark-up is calculated on the cost).

**iv) Rate of turnover**

$$\text{Average stock} = \dfrac{\text{opening stock} + \text{closing stock}}{2} = \dfrac{150{,}000 + 50{,}000}{2} = 100{,}000$$

$$\text{Rate of turnover} = \dfrac{\text{cost of goods sold}}{\text{average stock}} = \dfrac{600{,}000}{100{,}000} = 6 \text{ times}$$

The stock is sold and replaced **6 times** during the trading period.

| Item | Working | Result |
|---|---|---:|
| Gross profit | 25% of 600,000 | CFAF 150,000 |
| Net profit | 150,000 - 50,000 | CFAF 100,000 |
| Gross profit as % of sales | 150,000 / 750,000 x 100 | 20% |
| Rate of turnover | 600,000 / 100,000 | 6 times |

*Note.* The cost of goods sold (600,000) is given in the table, so it is used as printed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Name and explain any FOUR advantages of advertising to the economy.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Advertising is any paid message which informs and persuades people to buy goods or services. It brings the following advantages to the economy.

1. **It informs people about goods and services.** Advertising tells consumers what is available, where to buy and at what price, so they can choose well and save time.

2. **It increases demand and production.** When more people buy, firms produce more, so the output of the country increases and the economy grows.

3. **It creates employment.** More production needs more workers, and advertising itself gives jobs to artists, journalists, printers, radio and television staff, billboard makers and other persons.

4. **It lowers prices (economies of scale).** When production is large, the cost of each unit falls. The firm can then sell at lower prices, which benefits the consumers.

5. **It encourages competition and better quality.** Firms advertise to win customers, so they try to improve their goods and to launch new ones, and the consumer has more choice.

6. **It supports the media and brings revenue to the State.** Newspapers, radio and television receive income from advertising, and more business activity brings more taxes to the government.

**Conclusion.** Advertising helps trade to expand and the standard of living to improve.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline any FOUR government departments that protect consumers.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Consumers are protected by several government departments. Their exact names may differ, but the following kinds of department protect consumers.

1. **The ministry or department in charge of trade (consumer protection and price control).** It controls prices and trading practices and receives complaints from consumers.

2. **The ministry or department in charge of public health.** It inspects food, drugs, restaurants and markets to make sure that they are safe and hygienic.

3. **The national standards and quality control body.** It sets standards for goods and tests their quality and safety.

4. **The weights and measures service.** It checks scales, measures and packaged goods so that traders do not cheat on quantity.

5. **The customs department.** It stops fake, dangerous or prohibited goods from entering the country.

6. **The police and the courts.** They punish traders who cheat, sell dangerous goods or break the law on consumer protection.
